Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model: each observation is either a "structural zero" (with probability pi) or a draw from a negative binomial distribution, which can also produce zeros. The model is fitted with an EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits, written from scratch. No general-purpose optimizer is used. The parameterization and the coefficient names are those of pscl::zeroinfl(dist = "negbin").

Usage

zinbreg(
  formula,
  data,
  offset = NULL,
  control = zinbreg_control(),
  weights = NULL,
  subset,
  na.action,
  model = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before the bar, zero-model covariates after it. Use | 1 for a zero part with only an intercept. Without a bar (y ~ x1 + x2) the whole right-hand side, including any offset() terms, is used for both parts, as in pscl::zeroinfl(); to keep an offset in the count part only, write it before the bar (y ~ x + offset(log(t)) | x). offset() terms are allowed in either part. The response must contain non-negative whole numbers, with at least one zero.

data

A data frame (or list or environment) containing the variables in formula. If missing, variables are taken from the environment in which formula was created.

offset

Optional numeric vector added to the linear predictor of the count part, for example the log of an exposure time, with one value per row of data. It is added to any offset() terms of the count part. NULL (the default) means no offset argument.

control

A list of settings from zinbreg_control(). A plain list is also accepted and is checked by passing it to zinbreg_control().

weights

Optional non-negative prior weights, one per observation. Each observation's contribution to the log-likelihood is multiplied by its weight; a weight of 0 leaves it out.

subset

Optional expression selecting the rows of data to use.

na.action

How to handle missing values; defaults to getOption("na.action").

model

Logical; if TRUE (the default), the model frame is kept in the result.

...

Not used. Supplying anything here is an error, so that a misspelled argument is not silently ignored.

Value

An object of class zinbreg, a list containing:

coefficients

List with the count and zero coefficient vectors.

vcov

Covariance matrix of the count and zero coefficients, with names count_* and zero_*.

vcov_full

Covariance matrix including Log(theta).

theta, SE.theta, SE.logtheta

The dispersion estimate, its standard error (delta method) and the standard error of log(theta).

loglik, df

The maximized log-likelihood and the number of estimated parameters, \(p + q + 1\).

iter, converged

Number of EM iterations and whether the fit converged (see Details).

gradient, newton_decrement, gradient_check

The analytic gradient at the estimates, the Newton decrement, and the result of the gradient check.

mstep_status

Counts of M-steps that did not converge, failed to halve a step, were damped, were restarted and so on, over all iterations.

em_violations

Data frame of monotonicity violations (usually empty).

start_method

How the starting values were obtained.

theta_bound

"none", or "upper"/"lower" if theta ended on a bound.

diverging

Names (count_*, zero_*) of coefficients without a finite estimate.

fitted.values

The fitted means \((1 - \pi)\mu\).

mu, pi, linear.predictors

Count-part means, structural-zero probabilities, and the linear predictors of both parts (including offsets).

residuals

Response residuals \(y - (1 - \pi)\mu\).

prior.weights, offset, y, x, z

The weights, the offsets of both parts, the (rounded) response and the two model matrices.

nobs, df.residual

Number of observations with positive weight, and that number minus df.

loglik_trace

Log-likelihood after each EM iteration.

terms, model, xlevels, contrasts, na.action

Model frame information used by the methods.

hessian, hessian_difference

The Hessian method used and, with hessian_check = TRUE, the relative difference between the analytic and numeric Hessians.

offset_arg_used, formula, call, control

Whether the offset argument was supplied, the two-part formula, the matched call and the settings used.

Details

The model is $$P(Y_i = 0) = \pi_i + (1 - \pi_i) f_{NB}(0; \mu_i, \theta),$$ $$P(Y_i = y) = (1 - \pi_i) f_{NB}(y; \mu_i, \theta), \quad y \ge 1,$$ with \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\) and \(\mathrm{logit}\, \pi_i = z_i^\top \gamma + o^z_i\). Because it is a mixture, it is not a GLM, so IRLS cannot be applied to it directly.

The EM algorithm treats "is a structural zero" as missing data and repeats:

  • E-step: for each zero, compute the probability \(\tau_i\) that it is a structural zero (it is 0 for every positive count).

  • Zero M-step: a logistic IRLS fit of the fractional response \(\tau_i\) on the zero-part covariates. It never divides by \(\pi_i(1 - \pi_i)\), so it stays exact when probabilities are extremely close to 0 or 1, and it is damped when its weighted cross-product matrix is singular.

  • Count M-step: nbreg()'s algorithm with prior weights \(1 - \tau_i\).

Every iteration is checked: EM must never lower the log-likelihood, and neither M-step may lower its own part of the EM objective (generalized EM). The flags of every M-step are recorded.

EM converges slowly when the zero part is poorly determined, so small changes between iterations are not enough to stop. EM stops when the changes are small and the gradient check passes: the Newton decrement \(g^\top (-H)^{-1} g\) of the log-likelihood (analytic gradient and Hessian) must be at most grad_tol. The fit is reported as converged only if, in addition, the M-steps of the final iteration converged and no monotonicity violation occurred.

Standard errors come from the inverse of the negative Hessian of the observed-data log-likelihood in \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\): analytic by default, numeric on request (see zinbreg_control()).

Starting values come from a negative binomial fit for the count part and a logistic fit of I(y == 0) for the zero part (with fallbacks if that logistic fit separates), unless supplied with zinbreg_control(start = ).

Coefficients that run off to plus or minus infinity are detected per part and then held fixed; their standard errors are NA. See the section below.

Errors and warnings

Errors:

  • nbzinbreg_error_input: an invalid argument or invalid data. Besides the problems listed in nbreg() (formula, data, unused arguments, control, variables, offsets, weights, response values, model matrices), this covers a formula with more than one response or more than two right-hand parts, a count or zero part without coefficients, a response without any zero among the observations with positive weight (there is then nothing to model with the zero part; use nbreg()), a non-finite zero-part offset, too few observations for the \(p + q + 1\) parameters, and start values whose lengths or names do not match the model.

  • nbzinbreg_error_rank: columns of the count or zero model matrix are linear combinations of other columns (the message names the part and the columns).

  • nbzinbreg_error_fit: an unrecoverable numerical failure (the message gives the EM iteration).

Warnings (the fit is still returned):

  • nbzinbreg_warning_convergence: the fit did not converge, with the reason(s): EM reached maxit; the gradient check failed or could not be carried out; or an M-step of the final iteration did not converge. converged is then FALSE.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_monotone: EM lowered the log-likelihood, or an M-step lowered its part of the EM objective, beyond rounding error.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_theta: theta exceeds theta_warn, or ended on a bound (settings of nb_control).

  • nbzinbreg_warning_divergence: coefficients without a finite estimate, explained per part: a zero-part group with no zeros (its structural-zero probability goes to 0); a group whose counts are all zero (either part can absorb it, so it is not identified); other coefficients detected running off to infinity; or no zero inflation at all (every fitted probability of a structural zero below 1e-8; nbreg() may be adequate). Their estimates are not meaningful and their standard errors are NA.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_se: standard errors unavailable or possibly inaccurate (non-finite, asymmetric or ill-conditioned Hessian, a negative Hessian that is not positive definite, or analytic and numeric Hessians that disagree with hessian_check = TRUE).

See also

zinbreg_control(), nbreg(), zinbreg-methods

Examples

if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  fit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                 data = bioChemists)
  fit
  summary(fit)
}
